title: Act Four. Radha-abhisara (Radha's Tryst)
html:
Krishna, suffering in separation, repents of His pretence; Madanika tells Him of Radha's sufferings and at His request goes to bring her; Radha comes to the appointed grove; Krishna waits for her anxiously as the moon rises; the meeting.

(Enter Madanika.)

Madanika. Ah, I heard from Madana-manjari that Mukunda is sitting with the little brahmin at the foot of the vakula tree; I'll go there. (Looking ahead.) Ah, here is Mukunda, consulting dejectedly about something with the brahmin. Surely the Flower-arrowed One has been at play here. Let me hide behind the madhavi bush and listen. (She hides.)

(Enter Krishna, acting the state of one in love, talking with the jester.)

Madanika (aside).

Song 13 — in raga Malava.

Song 13 (2)

वदनमिदं विधुमण्डलमधुरं विधुरं बत सुचिरेण
कलयदनङ्गशराहतमनिशं मलिनमिवेन्दुकरेण ॥
माधववपुरतिखेदं
जनयति चेतसि शतधा भेदम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
परिहृतहारं हृदयमुदारं धूसरितं विरहेण
मरकतशैलशिलातलमाहतमहह किमिन्दुकरेण ॥
गजपतिरुद्रं सुकृतसमुद्रं शशिकिरणादपि शीतं
रामानन्दरायकविभणितं सुखयतु रुचिरं गीतम् ॥ २ ॥

vadanamidaṁ vidhumaṇḍalamadhuraṁ vidhuraṁ bata sucireṇa
kalayadanaṅgaśarāhatamaniśaṁ malinamivendukareṇa ||
mādhavavapuratikhedaṁ
janayati cetasi śatadhā bhedam || dhru ||
parihṛtahāraṁ hṛdayamudāraṁ dhūsaritaṁ viraheṇa
marakataśailaśilātalamāhatamahaha kimindukareṇa ||
gajapatirudraṁ sukṛtasamudraṁ śaśikiraṇādapi śītaṁ
rāmānandarāyakavibhaṇitaṁ sukhayatu ruciraṁ gītam || 2 ||

vadanam idam — this face; vidhu-maṇḍala-madhuram — sweet as the moon's orb; vidhuram — faded; bata — alas; sucireṇa — long since; kalayat — showing; anaṅga-śara-āhatam — struck by the Bodiless One's arrows; aniśam — ceaselessly; malinam — withered; iva — as if; indu-kareṇa — by a moonbeam; mādhava-vapuḥ — Madhava's body; ati-khedam — in great pain; janayati — produces; cetasi — in the heart; śatadhā — a hundredfold; bhedam — splitting; parihṛta-hāram — having cast off its necklace; hṛdayam — the chest; udāram — broad; dhūsaritam — greyed; viraheṇa — by separation; marakata-śaila-śilā-talam — an emerald rock-face; āhatam — struck; ahaha — ah; kim — is it; indu-kareṇa — by a moonbeam; gajapati-rudram — Gajapati Rudra; sukṛta-samudram — ocean of good deeds; śaśi-kiraṇāt api — than moonlight even; śītam — cooler; rāmānanda-rāya-kavi-bhaṇitam — spoken by the poet Ramananda Raya; sukhayatu — may it delight; ruciram — lovely; gītam — song.

2This face, sweet as the moon's orb — alas, it has long been faded, like a lotus struck by the moon's ray, wounded day and night by the arrows of the Bodiless One. The great pain of Madhava's body splits my heart in two, into a hundred pieces. (Refrain.) His broad chest, having cast off its necklace, has turned grey with separation — ah, is it an emerald rock struck by a moonbeam? May the lovely song spoken by the poet Ramananda Raya delight Gajapati Rudra, ocean of good deeds — cooler than moonlight.1

Krishna.

Verse 3

सा चेदुत्पललोचना सहचरीवक्त्रेण मे निर्भरं
प्रेमाणं प्रकटीचकार तदयं हासो मया कल्पितः ।
हाहा शुक्तिधिया महामणिरभूत्त्यक्तो मया दैवतो
यायाल्लोचनगोचरं पुनरियं पुण्यैरगण्यैर्मम ॥ ३ ॥

sā cedutpalalocanā sahacarīvaktreṇa me nirbharaṁ
premāṇaṁ prakaṭīcakāra tadayaṁ hāso mayā kalpitaḥ |
hāhā śuktidhiyā mahāmaṇirabhūttyakto mayā daivato
yāyāllocanagocaraṁ punariyaṁ puṇyairagaṇyairmama || 3 ||

sā — she; cet — if; utpala-locanā — lotus-eyed; sahacarī-vaktreṇa — through her friend's lips; me — to Me; nirbharam — boundless; premāṇam — love; prakaṭī-cakāra — revealed; tat — then; ayam — this; hāsaḥ — mockery; mayā — by Me; kalpitaḥ — contrived; hāhā — alas; śukti-dhiyā — thinking it a shell; mahā-maṇiḥ — a great jewel; abhūt tyaktaḥ — has been cast away; mayā — by Me; daivataḥ — by fate; yāyāt — may she come; locana-gocaram — within sight; punaḥ — again; iyam — she; puṇyaiḥ — by merits; agaṇyaiḥ — countless; mama — My.

3If that lotus-eyed one revealed to Me her boundless love through her friend's lips, and I contrived this mockery — alas, alas, I have thrown away a great jewel, thinking it a shell! If only by fate she might come again within sight of My eyes, through My countless merits!2

Jester (Prakrit). Hey friend, didn't I tell you not to reject this loving girl? Why do you pine now? When the appetite is gone, what's the use of laddus and sweets? So here I'm the only remedy.

Krishna. How so?

Jester (Prakrit). I'm a brahmin: I'll keep repeating a mantra over and over and draw her here!3

Krishna. I know your brahminhood. Look rather — here is Madanika.

Madanika (coming forward). Blessings on you, child.

Krishna (looking ahead). What, Madanika? (Respectfully.) Lady, welcome.

Madanika. Noble one, to see the moon of your face is all the welfare I need.

Jester (Prakrit). Our dear friend is tormented by the Flower-arrowed One; so bring that very cowherd girl!

Krishna (embarrassed). Fie, fool, don't talk like that!

Jester (Prakrit). We brahmins are simple folk — we speak plainly.

Madanika (smiling). Child, you are truthful indeed.

Jester (Prakrit). Of course! Look, look — here are lotus leaves! (He shows dry, rustling leaves. Then, using Sanskrit:)4

Song 14 — in raga Duhkhi-varadi.

Song 14 (15)

नलिनवनं वनमालिकृतेऽकृत(?) मुज्झितकुसुमपलाशं
पल्लवमपि वृन्दावनमनु कलयसि ललितविकाशम् ॥
सरले पश्यसि किमु न हि कृष्णं
त्वयि निहिताशं गलितविलासं चातकमिव घनतृष्णम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
विधुमिव वीक्ष्य विधुन्तुदमानय चपलमिति प्रतिवेलं
वदति कथं वद यदि मदनो हृदि न वसति विरचितखेलम् ॥
गजपतिरुद्रमुदं तनुतामिति रामानन्दरायसुगीतं
निभृतमनोभवविशिखपराभवहरिविरहेण समेतम् ॥ १५ ॥

nalinavanaṁ vanamālikṛte'kṛta(?) mujjhitakusumapalāśaṁ
pallavamapi vṛndāvanamanu kalayasi lalitavikāśam ||
sarale paśyasi kimu na hi kṛṣṇaṁ
tvayi nihitāśaṁ galitavilāsaṁ cātakamiva ghanatṛṣṇam || dhru ||
vidhumiva vīkṣya vidhuntudamānaya capalamiti prativelaṁ
vadati kathaṁ vada yadi madano hṛdi na vasati viracitakhelam ||
gajapatirudramudaṁ tanutāmiti rāmānandarāyasugītaṁ
nibhṛtamanobhavaviśikhaparābhavahariviraheṇa sametam || 15 ||

nalina-vanam — the lotus grove; vanamāli-kṛte — for the sake of Vanamali; ujjhita-kusuma-palāśam — bereft of flowers and petals; pallavam api — and the shoots; vṛndāvanam anu — in Vrindavana; kalayasi — you see; lalita-vikāśam — lovely and open; sarale — simple girl; paśyasi kimu na hi — do you not see; kṛṣṇam — Krishna; tvayi nihita-āśam — who has placed His hope in you; galita-vilāsam — who has given up play; cātakam iva — like a chataka; ghana-tṛṣṇam — thirsting for the cloud; vidhum — the moon; vīkṣya — seeing; vidhuntudam — Rahu; ānaya — bring; capalam — quickly; iti — thus; prativelam — constantly; vadati — says; katham — how; vada — tell; yadi — if; madanaḥ — Madana; hṛdi — in the heart; na vasati — does not dwell; viracita-khelam — staging games; gajapati-rudra-mudam — the joy of Gajapati Rudra; tanutām — may it increase; iti — thus; rāmānanda-rāya-su-gītam — Ramananda Raya's fine song; nibhṛta-manobhava-viśikha-parābhava-hari-viraheṇa — with separation from Hari, secretly vanquished by the arrows of the Mind-born; sametam — filled.

15In the lotus grove not a flower, not a petal is left, for the sake of Vanamali; and in Vrindavana you see only lovely opening shoots. Simple girl, don't you see Krishna? He has placed all His hope in you, forgotten His play — like a chataka bird thirsting for the cloud. (Refrain.) Looking at the moon, He keeps saying: "Bring Rahu quickly!" — tell me, how could He speak so if Madana were not dwelling in His heart, staging his games?5 May this fine song of Ramananda Raya, full of separation from Hari, who is secretly vanquished by the arrows of the Mind-born, increase the joy of Gajapati Rudra.

Madanika. Is that all?

Jester (Prakrit). You've become our dear friend's friend, yet you don't understand even what's been said. Very well, I'll go myself and bring her — I too am an envoy with full powers! (He starts to go.)

Krishna (catches him by his upper cloth).

Madanika. Child Krishna, why hide anything from me?

Krishna. Lady, I want to ask you something.

Madanika. Speak freely.

Krishna.

Verse 22

तत्रास्यास्तस्या(?) वदनरुचमाकर्ण्य शशिनः
कृतावज्ञां यस्मादयमपि रुजं तद्वितनुताम् ।
तदङ्गे नासङ्गं भजत इति यो मे बहुमतः
कथं सोऽपि प्राणैर्मम मलयवातो विहरति ॥ २२ ॥

tatrāsyāstasyā(?) vadanarucamākarṇya śaśinaḥ
kṛtāvajñāṁ yasmādayamapi rujaṁ tadvitanutām |
tadaṅge nāsaṅgaṁ bhajata iti yo me bahumataḥ
kathaṁ so'pi prāṇairmama malayavāto viharati || 22 ||

yasmāt — since; ākarṇya — having heard; śaśinaḥ — of the moon; vadana-rucam — the lustre of the face; kṛta-avajñām — scorned (by her); ayam api — let it too; rujam — pain; vitanutām — cause; tad-aṅge — her body's; āsaṅgam — touch; bhajate — enjoys; iti — because; yaḥ — which; me — by Me; bahu-mataḥ — highly prized; katham — how; saḥ api — it too; prāṇaiḥ — with the life; mama — My; malaya-vātaḥ — the Malaya breeze; viharati — plays.

22Ever since you told Me that she scorns the lustre of the moon's face — let the moon torment Me! But the Malaya breeze, which I prized so much because it touches her body — how can it too toy with My life?6

Madanika (aside). Radhika's wish has been fulfilled together with ours. Let me tell Him of her pain of separation too. (Aloud.) Child, of that lovely one too only her beauty remains. For:

Verse 24

शिलापट्टे हैमे तुहिनकिरणं चन्दनरसै-
रियं तन्वी पिष्ट्वा तनुमनु विलेपं मृगयते ।
क्षणं स्थित्वा हाहा सरसबिसिनीपत्रशयने
समुत्तस्थौ यावज्ज्वलति न चिरान्मर्मरमिदम् ॥ २४ ॥

śilāpaṭṭe haime tuhinakiraṇaṁ candanarasai-
riyaṁ tanvī piṣṭvā tanumanu vilepaṁ mṛgayate |
kṣaṇaṁ sthitvā hāhā sarasabisinīpatraśayane
samuttasthau yāvajjvalati na cirānmarmaramidam || 24 ||

śilā-paṭṭe — on a slab; haime — golden; tuhina-kiraṇam — the cool-rayed (camphor); candana-rasaiḥ — with sandal juice; iyam — this; tanvī — slender one; piṣṭvā — having ground; tanum anu — for the body; vilepam — ointment; mṛgayate — seeks; kṣaṇam — a moment; sthitvā — staying; hāhā — alas; sarasa-bisinī-patra-śayane — on a bed of juicy lotus leaves; samuttasthau — rose up; yāvat — before; jvalati na — catches fire; cirāt — soon; marmaram — rustling; idam — this.

24This slender one, grinding sandal and cool moon on a golden stone slab, seeks something to anoint her body. Pausing a moment — alas, alas! — she rose from her bed of juicy lotus leaves before they could catch fire and start to rustle.7

Song 15 — in raga Sama-todi.

Song 15 (25)

निरवधिनयनसलिलभवसादे
पतति कृशा परिचलति च पादे ॥
माधव गुरुतरमनसिजबाधा
हरि हरि कथमपि जीवति राधा ॥ ध्रु ॥
निवससि चेतसि कथमिव वामं
शिव शिव शमयसि तदपि न कामम् ॥
गजपतिरुद्रनृपतिमविगीतं
सुखयतु रामानन्दसुगीतम् ॥ २५ ॥

niravadhinayanasalilabhavasāde
patati kṛśā paricalati ca pāde ||
mādhava gurutaramanasijabādhā
hari hari kathamapi jīvati rādhā || dhru ||
nivasasi cetasi kathamiva vāmaṁ
śiva śiva śamayasi tadapi na kāmam ||
gajapatirudranṛpatimavigītaṁ
sukhayatu rāmānandasugītam || 25 ||

niravadhi-nayana-salila-bhava-sāde — in the mire born of endless tears; patati — falls; kṛśā — emaciated; paricalati — slips; ca — and; pāde — her foot; mādhava — O Madhava; gurutara-manasija-bādhā — heavy is love's pain; hari hari — Hari, Hari; katham api — barely; jīvati — lives; rādhā — Radha; nivasasi — You dwell; cetasi — in the heart; katham iva — how; vāmam — perversely; śiva śiva — O Shiva, Shiva; śamayasi na — You do not quench; tad api — still; kāmam — her longing; gajapati-rudra-nṛpatim — King Gajapati Rudra; avigītam — flawless; sukhayatu — may it delight; rāmānanda-sugītam — Ramananda's fine song.

25Emaciated, she falls in the mire endlessly made by the tears of her eyes, and her feet slip. Madhava, the pain of love is heavy! Hari, Hari, Radha is barely alive. (Refrain.) How do You dwell in her heart — and yet torment it? O Shiva, Shiva, and still You do not quench her longing!8 May Ramananda's flawless song delight King Gajapati Rudra.

Jester (Prakrit). Lady, I reckon cowherd girls are reckless: they go looking for ointment of moon and sandal. But our dear friend, seeing the moon, hides his body somewhere and sits with his eyes shut, like an owl before the sun; and if he catches even a breath of sandal-wind, he darts this way and that like a snake at a potent spell.9

Krishna (aside). Well said. (Aloud.) Fie, fool, don't chatter so!

Madanika. How many rules of duty were not preached to her to test her heart!

Krishna (aside, anxiously). Can she have turned away from her longing for Me?

Madanika. So then:

Verse 30

यदा नासौ दोषं गणयति गुरूणां कुवचने
न वा तोषं धत्ते सरसवचने नर्म सुहृदाम् ।
विषाभं श्रीखण्डं कलयति विधुं पावकसमं
तदास्यास्तद्वृत्तं त्वयि गदितुमत्राहमगमम् ॥ ३० ॥

yadā nāsau doṣaṁ gaṇayati gurūṇāṁ kuvacane
na vā toṣaṁ dhatte sarasavacane narma suhṛdām |
viṣābhaṁ śrīkhaṇḍaṁ kalayati vidhuṁ pāvakasamaṁ
tadāsyāstadvṛttaṁ tvayi gaditumatrāhamagamam || 30 ||

yadā — when; na — not; asau — she; doṣam — as fault; gaṇayati — counts; gurūṇām — of the elders; kuvacane — in harsh words; na vā — nor; toṣam — pleasure; dhatte — takes; sarasa-vacane — in words full of rasa; narma — jests; suhṛdām — of friends; viṣa-ābham — like poison; śrī-khaṇḍam — sandal; kalayati — regards; vidhum — the moon; pāvaka-samam — like fire; tadā — then; asyāḥ — her; tad-vṛttam — that state; tvayi — to You; gaditum — to tell; atra — here; aham — I; agamam — came.

30when she disregards the rebukes of her elders, when she takes no pleasure in her friends' jests full of rasa, when she sees sandal as poison and the moon as fire — then I came here to tell You of her state.10

Krishna (with a sigh of relief).

Verse 31

त्वं चेदवञ्चनपरा(?) स्मरवारिराशे-
रुद्धर्तुमपि तदकारणवत्सलासि ।
तत्केशरद्रुमनिकुञ्जगृहे प्रसाद्य
तामानयस्व नय कोविदतां तनुष्व ॥ ३१ ॥

tvaṁ cedavañcanaparā(?) smaravārirāśe-
ruddhartumapi tadakāraṇavatsalāsi |
tatkeśaradrumanikuñjagṛhe prasādya
tāmānayasva naya kovidatāṁ tanuṣva || 31 ||

tvam — you; cet — if; avañcana-parā — a stranger to deceit; smara-vāri-rāśeḥ — from the ocean of Smara; uddhartum — to draw out; api — even; tat — then; akāraṇa-vatsalā — causelessly loving; asi — you are; tat — so; keśara-druma-nikuñja-gṛhe — to the bower-house by the keshara tree; prasādya — winning over; tām — her; ānayasva — bring; naya-kovidatām — skill in management; tanuṣva — display.

31Since you, a stranger to deceit, in causeless affection would draw Me out even from the ocean of Smara — then win her over and bring her to the bower-house by the keshara tree. Show your skill!11

Madanika. Child, it shall be so.

Jester (Prakrit). Simple lady, this is true indeed — I, a brahmin, stand surety for it.

Krishna. Enough of doubts — accomplish My cause.

Madanika. Here I go. Blessings on you, child. (Exit.)

(Enter Radhika, dressed for the tryst.)

Radha (Prakrit). Friend Madhavi, you have deceived me!

Song 16 — in raga Ramakeli.

Song 16 (37)

तिमिरतिरोहितसरणी
गिरिषु दरीषु समेव हि धरणी ॥
चिरयति किं सखि देवी
विधिरपि मयि किमु न हि हितसेवी ॥ ध्रु ॥
अतिवाहितमतिभीमं
विफलमिदं किमु गहनमसीमम् ॥
सुखयतु रुद्रगजेशं
रामानन्दरायकृतमनिशम् ॥ ३७ ॥

timiratirohitasaraṇī
giriṣu darīṣu sameva hi dharaṇī ||
cirayati kiṁ sakhi devī
vidhirapi mayi kimu na hi hitasevī || dhru ||
ativāhitamatibhīmaṁ
viphalamidaṁ kimu gahanamasīmam ||
sukhayatu rudragajeśaṁ
rāmānandarāyakṛtamaniśam || 37 ||

timira-tirohita-saraṇī — the path hidden by darkness; giriṣu — on mountains; darīṣu — in caves; samā eva — level; hi — indeed; dharaṇī — the ground; cirayati — delays; kim — why; sakhi — friend; devī — the lady; vidhiḥ api — Fate too; mayi — to me; kimu na hi — does not; hita-sevī — wish well; ativāhitam — crossed; ati-bhīmam — fearful; viphalam — in vain; idam — this; kimu — is it; gahanam — dense forest; asīmam — boundless; sukhayatu — may it delight; rudra-gajeśam — Rudra, lord of elephants; rāmānanda-rāya-kṛtam — made by Ramananda Raya; aniśam — ever.

37The path is hidden in darkness; mountains and caves — all have become level ground.
Why, friend, does the lady delay? Does even Fate not wish me well? (Refrain.)
Have I crossed this fearful, boundless, dense forest in vain?
May this, made by Ramananda Raya, ever delight Rudra, lord of elephants.12

Madhavi. Friend, enough of doubts: take it that the lady has already come.

(Enter Madanika.)

Madanika. Child, fortune smiles on you!

Radha (with a joyful sigh, Prakrit). Lady, what news from there?

Madanika. Such as there is in a violent fever of love.

Radha (Prakrit). How so?

Madanika.

Verse 43

इन्दुं निन्दति चन्दनं विकिरति प्रालम्बकं मुञ्चति
प्रालेयात्त्रसति प्रियं परिजनं नाभाषते सम्प्रति ।
गोविन्दस्तव विप्रयोगविधुरः किं किं न वा चेष्टते
तत्कुञ्जोदरतल्पकल्पनपरं राधे तमाराधय ॥ ४३ ॥

induṁ nindati candanaṁ vikirati prālambakaṁ muñcati
prāleyāttrasati priyaṁ parijanaṁ nābhāṣate samprati |
govindastava viprayogavidhuraḥ kiṁ kiṁ na vā ceṣṭate
tatkuñjodaratalpakalpanaparaṁ rādhe tamārādhaya || 43 ||

indum — the moon; nindati — reviles; candanam — sandal; vikirati — scatters; prālambakam — the long necklace; muñcati — casts off; prāleyāt — at the dew; trasati — trembles; priyam — dear; parijanam — companions; na ābhāṣate — does not speak to; samprati — now; govindaḥ — Govinda; tava — from you; viprayoga-vidhuraḥ — afflicted by separation; kiṁ kiṁ na vā — what does He not; ceṣṭate — do; tat — so; kuñja-udara-talpa-kalpana-param — intent on preparing a bed in the heart of the bower; rādhe — O Radha; tam — Him; ārādhaya — gladden.

✦

Notes

  1. Madanika sees Krishna suffering in separation. His face has faded like a lotus under the moon (the lotus closes at night), and His dark chest is compared to an emerald rock. The first word of the song is printed "madana" ("Kama"); by the sense and the Hindi translation we read "vadana" ("face"). The last line is unclear.
  2. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Krishna repents of His feigned refusal (Act 2). "Thrown away a jewel, thinking it a shell" is a proverbial image. There is no stage direction here in the Sanskrit text.
  3. The jester jokes that as a brahmin he will "draw" Radha by an attraction-spell (ākarṣaṇa).
  4. The jester shows Madanika dry leaves: everything fresh in the forest has already been gathered for cooling beds for the suffering Krishna. The direction "using Sanskrit" refers to the following song (sung by the jester or Madanika; the edition does not name the character).
  5. Rahu is the demon who swallows the moon at an eclipse. In separation Krishna cannot bear the moonlight and calls for Rahu to "swallow" the moon. The first line of the song is corrupt in the print and is rendered by the sense and the edition's Hindi translation.
  6. Śikhariṇī metre. The beginning of the verse is corrupt in the print. Krishna loved the Malaya breeze because it touches Radha, but now, in separation, the breeze torments Him too.
  7. Signs of the "fever of love" (madana-jvara): Radha seeks cooling with sandal, "cool moon" (camphor) and lotus leaves, but the heat of her body is such that the leaves wither and rustle.
  8. "Torment" — printed vāmam, "perversely, hostilely" (Hindi: "being crooked"). Krishna dwells in Radha's heart and yet does not quench her longing — a sign of the highest love in separation (vipralambha).
  9. The jester compares Radha's and Krishna's sufferings. The owl cannot bear the sun and the snake flees from the charmer's spell; to Krishna in separation the moon and sandal are unbearable.
  10. Śikhariṇī metre. Madanika relates that Radha was tested with intimidation and reminders of duty (cf. Act 3, Shashimukhi), but her love did not waver — a sign of anurāga, unwavering love that knows no obstacles.
  11. Vasanta-tilakā metre (printed as prose in the edition). "Causeless" (akāraṇa-vatsalā) — the friend's selfless love for both lovers, as Rupa Gosvami describes the sakhis, who are happy only in the union of Radha and Krishna.
  12. Radha has come to the place of the tryst (abhisāra) at night through the dark forest — in poetics an abhisārikā, a heroine going to her lover. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition her journey through darkness and danger is an image of all-conquering prema, which takes no account of any obstacle.
  13. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. The print has prāleyāṁtra sati, read as prāleyāt trasati, "shrinks from the dew".
  14. Śikhariṇī metre. "Here love alone is the refuge" (kāmo 'tra śaraṇam): kāma here is the same prema (CC Adi 4.163).
  15. At night the cakravakas are parted and cry, night-lilies open and day-lotuses close — all signs of moonrise. The eastern mountain (Udayagiri) is the mountain behind which, by tradition, the sun and moon rise.
  16. The moonlight will betray Radha, dressed in dark clothes for a night tryst (tamisrābhisārikā). "Eastern quarter" — literally "the quarter of Shakra", that is, of Indra.
  17. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. A charming scene of uncertainty (sandeha): Krishna at first mistakes the sound of Radha's anklets for other sounds.
  18. Madhu-mathana — "Slayer of Madhu", Krishna. The garland is a sign of choosing the beloved. In the last line King Prataparudra is called "the new Madana of our time" — courtly praise of his beauty. The words "bid the Bodiless One dance" are unclear in the print (nartitumatanumanāmaṁ).
